prompt: CHALLENGE: Toluene (PhCH₃) + Cl₂/hν gives ~95% benzyl chloride (PhCH₂Cl) and essentially no ring chlorination. Yet Cl₂ is normally considered an UNSELECTIVE radical halogenator. Why the dramatic selectivity here?

options.label: Benzylic C–H BDE (~90 kcal/mol) is ~15 kcal/mol WEAKER than aromatic C–H and well below typical sp³ C–H. The benzylic radical is heavily resonance-stabilized, so even 'unselective' Cl• strongly prefers the benzylic position.
Chlorine is too big for the ring.
Cl₂ requires FeCl₃ to do ring halogenation; without a Lewis acid, no ring reaction can happen.

explanation: Cl• is 'unselective' only when comparing closely-matched sp³ C–H bonds. Benzylic C–H is in a different league because the resulting benzyl radical delocalizes into the ring (4 resonance structures). The energetic preference overwhelms Cl₂'s early TS. Ring chlorination also fails without a Lewis acid catalyst.
